newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler boss urges Europe to work toward EMU.
newsitem.headline: Daimler boss urges Europe to work toward EMU.

text.p: Daimler-Benz chairman Juergen Schrempp urged Europe to make greater efforts to forge currency union, warning against the high cost of giving up on the project half way through.
In an article written for Reuters, Schrempp said debate about the advantages of EMU, the number of participants and whether the project should be delayed are misplaced.

"It is not just about the possible advantages of currency union. Rather, it is also about the costs of a 'no-Euro scenario," Schrempp said. "For us, there is no alternative but to continue European integration and for currency union to take place."

Schrempp warned that if European Economic and Monetary Union is not achieved there could be loss of public confidence in countries now striving to meet EMU criteria and a "massive upward" revaluation of currencies in countries like Germany and France.

The Daimler chairman also said EMU states should not be afraid to take advantage of the flexibility the Maastricht Treaty provides for in meeting the criteria, but that stability should remain the main goal.

"I am not talking about easing the stability criteria. But the Maastricht Treaty has provided room for manoeuvre. The contract intentionally provides for flexibility -- flexibility that should be used in a way that will keep stability in mind," he wrote.
